solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Old lady beginning to think breaks are important (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of 'think' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.breaks: the T breaks into MATER, splitting it

blocks.note: mater is Latin for mother, old public-school slang for one's mum
first letter of 'think'

annotation.surface: Someone muses that an old woman's thinking breaks are what really count.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'breaks' a noun, as in rest breaks; in the wordplay it is a verb, with the T breaking the old lady in two. 'Matter' is the verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things that matter carry weight, and the verb is plural to agree with 'are'.

entries.clue: Current diverted to power plant? (8)

blocks.note: the surface wants an electric current; the setter means a stream of water led off a river
the surface wants a power station; the plant is a mill, driven by that water

annotation.surface: An electrical current rerouted to supply a power station.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests electricity and a power station, but the current is water and the plant is a mill, whose wheel it turns.
annotation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of water led off a river to turn a mill wheel, and a mill is a plant in the factory sense.

entries.clue: Will author prove a rubbish revolutionary? (8)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: something that revolves turns round, so ROT reads backwards

blocks.note: to prove something is to test it, as in 'the proof of the pudding'
as written
rot = nonsense, rubbish

annotation.surface: Could a writer called Will turn out to be a worthless radical?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Will' is capitalised to look like a first name, but it is a legal will.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal term: the person who draws up a will is, in law, its author.

entries.clue: Bloomer crust snatched from naughty kids (5)

indicatorNotes.crust snatched from: the crust is the outside, so the outer letters are taken away

blocks.note: little terrors = naughty children; lose the first and last letters

annotation.surface: Naughty children grab the crust off a loaf of bread.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf, which is why the crust fits the surface; it is also slang for a blunder.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: a bloomer is an embarrassing blunder.

entries.clue: Odds of a race finish paying out (8)

blocks.note: SP = starting price, the odds on a horse when the race begins
a finish is an ending

annotation.surface: A punter looks at the odds and the finish of a race that pays out.
annotation.walkthrough: SP is betting shorthand for starting price. 'Paying out' looks like the bookie settling winning bets, but it simply means laying out money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: laying out money on things, with the same -ing form as the clue.

entries.clue: Polish rock musician’s gift (7,5)

blocks.note: to polish a skill is to perfect it
a ship in heavy seas rocks, or pitches

annotation.surface: A rock guitarist from Poland has real talent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest the nationality, and 'rock musician' reads as one phrase, but it splits: rock is a verb, and musician starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the rare ability to name or sing any note unaided, an inborn gift of some musicians.

entries.clue: I fear messing with intelligence gathering is wicked (9)

indicatorNotes.gathering: to gather something is to take it in, so NOUS takes the scrambled letters into its middle

blocks.note: nous = common sense, intelligence
the letters rearranged, to sit after the N of NOUS

annotation.surface: Someone worries that interfering with intelligence-gathering is evil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence gathering' reads as spying, but it splits: the intelligence is the container, and 'gathering' tells it to hold the jumbled letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: wicked and villainous, usually of schemes.

entries.clue: Dripping, frozen and not used in Icelandic cooking (6)

indicatorNotes.not used in: 'and' is not used, so those letters are taken out of ICELANDIC
indicatorNotes.cooking: cooking mixes up the remaining letters

blocks.note: the word as printed
these three letters are removed, leaving ICELIC

annotation.surface: In Icelandic cuisine, the drippings are frozen and never used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dripping' looks like the cooking fat, fitting the kitchen surface, but it means dripping water.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a spike of ice formed as dripping water freezes.

entries.clue: It stops blood swelling in a gland (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a hole is to plug it, so IT plugs the middle of the blood

blocks.note: gore = spilt blood
as written; it goes in after the second letter

annotation.surface: Something that halts bleeding is found in a swollen gland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It stops blood' reads like a description of a clotting agent, but 'It' is simply a letter pair plugged into the blood.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical definition: an enlargement of the thyroid gland, seen as a swelling in the neck.

entries.clue: Result after playing with brilliance (6)

indicatorNotes.after playing: letters that have been played with are shuffled

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A match result after a brilliant performance.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sports report; 'playing' sounds like the game itself but only rearranges the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a gleam or sheen, and figuratively glory.

entries.clue: Service well covered by serviceman’s scribblings (8)

indicatorNotes.covered by: a cover goes round the outside, so the serviceman's letters sit one on each side

blocks.note: GI = an American soldier
the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services
fit and well = healthy

annotation.surface: A soldier writes notes about a church service and a well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a church service beside a water well; both are military and medical instead: an air force and good health.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: scribblings or drawings on public walls.

entries.clue: Feeling less than trendy (12)

blocks.note: under = less than, as in under ten
current = up to date, fashionable

annotation.surface: A sense of not being quite fashionable enough.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one feeling, but 'Feeling' is the definition and the rest builds the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a hidden feeling running beneath the surface, as in an undercurrent of resentment.

entries.clue: Move around behind class (9)

blocks.note: the rear is the behind
a range is a class or category, as in a price range

annotation.surface: A pupil shifts places to the back of the classroom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a schoolroom, but class means a category of things, not pupils.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shift things into new positions.

entries.clue: One all-powerful measure (5)

blocks.note: a sovereign, who holds all the power
a straight edge marked for measuring

annotation.surface: A single all-powerful yardstick.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but it splits after 'all-powerful'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a monarch who holds power, and the marked stick used to measure.

entries.clue: Representative sample of fake notices on X (5,7)

indicatorNotes.fake: fake notices are false versions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an X is a cross
NOTICES rearranged

annotation.surface: A sample of forged notices posted on X, the social network.
annotation.walkthrough: X looks like the social media platform, but it is just the shape of the letter. In an across clue, 'on' puts one piece before the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A statistical sense: a sample chosen to be typical of the whole.

entries.clue: Poking fun about attending a trial is terrible (9)

indicatorNotes.terrible: a terrible arrangement is a jumbled one

blocks.note: c = circa, about
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Making fun of people going to a court case is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is the Latin circa, abbreviated C, and it joins the letters of 'a trial is' before they are mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mocking through ridicule, and like 'poking fun' it describes a manner.

entries.clue: Cost, perhaps, without charge (4,4)

blocks.note: scot is an old word for a tax or payment, one kind of cost
free = costing nothing

annotation.surface: Something costs nothing, apparently.
annotation.walkthrough: SCOT survives only in this phrase: going scot-free first meant escaping the tax. So the whole clue both builds the answer and says what it means.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: escaping without charge or penalty, literally free of the scot, the payment due.

entries.clue: Hungry mutineers ousting the leader at sea (8)

indicatorNotes.ousting the leader: the first letter, M, is thrown out
indicatorNotes.at sea: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: MUTINEERS loses its first letter

annotation.surface: Starving sailors mutiny and throw their captain overboard.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a mutiny on the high seas, where ousting the leader means the captain; in the wordplay the leader is just the letter M.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: hungry or greedy, from the Latin for being hungry.

entries.clue: Some creatures stay in groups (5,7)

blocks.note: stick = stay put, as in stick around
as written
sects are religious or political groups

annotation.surface: Some animals keep together in herds.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests herd animals, but the answer is the insect that stays motionless to pass as a twig.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: twig-like insects are some of the world's creatures, hence the vague 'some'.

entries.clue: Lyrical work raising name to the top (6)

indicatorNotes.raising: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters so they read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.to the top: the letters go up to the top of the entry, reading upwards

blocks.note: to cite is to name, as in citing an example
op = opus, a work

annotation.surface: A songwriter's work puts a name in the headline.
annotation.walkthrough: The two pieces sit one after the other and the whole string is read upwards, so the work ends up on top.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: expressive in the manner of verse or song.

entries.clue: Break that is this chap’s first in months (6)

blocks.note: sc. = scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'
his = belonging to this chap
first letter

annotation.surface: A man takes his first holiday in months.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Break' a holiday; it is a split. The Latin abbreviation is rarer than i.e. but a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a split or rupture, especially within a church.

entries.clue: Statuesque figure given stretched limousine? (5)

blocks.note: OS = outsize, the clothing size, and a stretched thing is outsize
a limousine is a car

annotation.surface: A film star arrives at an awards night in a stretch limo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Statuesque' suggests a tall, elegant star, but the figure is literally a statuette: the award itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on 'statuesque': the gold statuette of the Academy Awards is a figure that really is a statue.

entries.clue: Reader, I married him in Kentish Town (9)

blocks.note: the famous line from Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre, about the hero she marries
a cathedral town in the county of Kent

annotation.surface: A narrator tells the reader about her wedding in a north London district.
annotation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real district of north London, so the phrase reads as a place name; here it just means a town in Kent.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: Jane Eyre's husband, Mr Rochester, and the Kent town on the River Medway.

entries.clue: Collection of bones after beheading the king (5)

indicatorNotes.beheading: the head, the first letter, is cut off

blocks.note: the pelvis is a ring of bones; lose its first letter

annotation.surface: Bones found after a king was executed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a royal execution, but 'the king' is the King of rock and roll, whose hip-shaking made his pelvis famous.
annotation.definitionFit: A nickname: Presley was billed as the King of Rock and Roll, usually just the King.

entries.clue: Rebel surrounded by fools and jerks (8)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: something surrounded is enclosed on all sides, so the rebel sits inside the fools

blocks.note: twits = fools
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary; goes in before the final S

annotation.surface: A rebel finds himself among idiots and fools.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like another word for fools, which is where the surface wants it, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sudden small movements, as a verb in the third person like 'jerks'.

entries.clue: Reluctant farewell oddly rushed (6)

blocks.note: ave is Latin for hail or farewell
letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'rushed'

annotation.surface: Someone unwilling to go says a hurried goodbye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as 'strangely' in the surface, but it means taking the odd letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unwilling, set against something.

entries.clue: Unqualified learner put into battle (8)

indicatorNotes.put into: to put a thing into another is to place it inside, so the learner goes inside the battle

blocks.note: to battle is to compete
L = learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car; goes in after the fourth letter

annotation.surface: An untrained novice sent into combat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified learner' reads as a trainee, but 'Unqualified' is the definition in the sense of total, as in unqualified success.
annotation.definitionFit: A sense of 'unqualified': without reservation, total, as in unqualified support.

entries.clue: Approval and the way it was conveyed (6)

blocks.note: as = the way, as in 'do it as I do'
something conveyed was sent

annotation.surface: Permission was granted, and it matters how it was passed on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one thought about how approval is delivered; 'and' is the seam between definition and wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: formal agreement, as in royal assent to a bill.
